Anonymous with CAPTCHA
Authenticate with Microsoft
Authenticate manually with Generic OAuth 2
questions.explanation: New agents default to 'Authenticate with Microsoft', which works in Teams, SharePoint, Power Apps and Microsoft Copilot. It doesn't expose User.AccessToken and can't be used with Dynamics 365 Customer Service.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: What's the risk of the 'No authentication' option in Copilot Studio?
choices: Every message is billed at the tenant graph grounding rate of 10 credits
The agent can only answer from public websites, never from internal knowledge
Anyone with the link can use it, and sharing can't limit who in the org does
The agent is automatically unpublished after 30 days without sign-ins
questions.explanation: With No authentication, anyone who has the link can interact with the agent. Classic chatbots default to it. Combined with internal knowledge sources, this is the main oversharing risk in Copilot Studio, so pair a data policy block with maker training.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Which authentication option is needed when an agent must call downstream APIs with the user's own token (User.AccessToken)?
choices: Authenticate with Microsoft, which passes the user's token to every tool automatically
No authentication, with the token passed in the URL
Authenticate manually (for example Entra ID V2 or Generic OAuth 2)
Any of the options; the token is always available
questions.explanation: Only manual authentication (Entra ID V2 with federated credentials, certificates or secrets; Entra ID; or Generic OAuth 2) exposes User.AccessToken. Switching an agent to 'Authenticate with Microsoft' turns User.AccessToken references into unknown variables and breaks tools that relied on them.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: A maker changes an agent's authentication setting. When does the change take effect for users?
choices: After the tenant admin approves it in Agent 365
After 24 hours of cache expiry
Immediately, for all channels
Only after the agent is published again
questions.explanation: Authentication changes only take effect after publishing. A security fix that isn't republished hasn't actually fixed anything.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Which Power Platform admin control stops makers from publishing generative AI agents at all?
choices: The Copilot Studio authors security group
Restricted SharePoint Search, applied to every environment that hosts generative AI agents
Customer Lockbox
'Disable agent publishing' for generative AI agents
questions.explanation: The security and governance guide lists a 'Disable agent publishing' control for generative AI agents in the Power Platform admin center, alongside disabling cross-geo data movement, environment routing, maker security scans and credit caps.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: A European customer wants Copilot Studio's generative AI features to stay in-region. Which admin control is relevant?
choices: Defender for Cloud Apps session policies on the Copilot Studio portal
Restricted Content Discovery on every SharePoint site used as knowledge, applied tenant-wide for the EU
'Disable data movement across geographic locations' for generative AI features
Copilot connector index quotas set per environment and region
questions.explanation: Copilot Studio offers a control to disable data movement across geographic locations for generative AI features outside the US. Data residency settings are worth comparing directly: Genie has its own cross-Geo processing setting at the workspace level.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Where are Copilot Studio maker audit logs available?
choices: In Microsoft Purview, with alerting possible through Microsoft Sentinel
Only through Power BI exports of the Dataverse audit table
Only in Copilot Studio's built-in analytics page for each agent, kept for 30 days with no export option
Only to Microsoft support engineers through Customer Lockbox
questions.explanation: Maker activities are logged to Microsoft Purview audit, and Sentinel can alert on them. Agent 365 adds identity and governance controls such as Entra Conditional Access and network controls.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Which data does Customer Lockbox not cover, according to Copilot Studio's security and governance guide?
choices: Dataverse tables that Copilot Studio agents read from or write to, and the SharePoint files they use as knowledge
SharePoint sites and files that agents use as knowledge sources
Teams chats and channel messages where users talk to agents
Copilot Studio security audit logging telemetry and Agent 365 governance events
questions.explanation: Microsoft notes that Customer Lockbox doesn't cover Copilot Studio security audit logging telemetry or Agent 365 governance events. Regulated customers who require Lockbox coverage need to know this.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Can admins encrypt Copilot Studio environment data with their own keys?
choices: Only when environment data is stored on a Fabric F64 capacity
Yes. Customer-managed keys (CMK) can be enabled for Copilot Studio environments
Only for agents published to public websites through Direct Line
No. Copilot Studio supports only Microsoft-managed keys, although Dataverse tables used by agents can use CMK
questions.explanation: Copilot Studio supports customer-managed encryption keys at the environment level. CMK is often a hard requirement in financial services and healthcare, so confirm it early with whichever platform the customer chooses.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: What can't a tenant-wide Copilot Studio policy do, per Microsoft's security guide?
choices: Block agents that use no authentication
Block conversations about arbitrary admin-defined subjects
Block makers from publishing agents to Microsoft Teams
Block agents from making outbound HTTP calls
questions.explanation: Microsoft notes a tenant-wide policy can't block conversations by arbitrary admin-defined subjects. Topic restrictions have to be designed into each agent's instructions and content moderation. Platform DLP governs connectors and channels, not conversation topics.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: How do you add an Azure Databricks Genie Agent to a Copilot Studio agent?
choices: Upload a CSV export of the Genie Agent's tables as a knowledge file, then refresh it on a schedule with an agent flow
Add the 'Azure Databricks Genie' MCP tool under Tools, then enter the Genie Agent ID
Add the Genie Agent's URL as a SharePoint knowledge source
Install the Genie app from AppSource into the Copilot Studio environment
questions.explanation: Azure Databricks docs: create a blank agent, go to Tools > + Add a Tool, search 'Azure Databricks' or choose Model Context Protocol, select 'Azure Databricks Genie', choose the connection, enter the Genie Agent ID, save, make sure generative orchestration is on, and publish. It requires the workspace's 'Managed MCP Servers' preview.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: What orchestration setting must be on for a Copilot Studio agent to use the Azure Databricks Genie tool?
choices: Deep reasoning mode
Proactive messaging
Generative (AI) orchestration
Classic topic-only orchestration
questions.explanation: The setup steps say to set Settings > Orchestration to Yes (generative AI orchestration) so the agent decides when to call Genie. Generative orchestration also generates agent actions and generative answers, so each Genie call carries credit cost for unlicensed or autonomous use.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Which instruction does Databricks recommend adding to a Copilot Studio agent that uses Genie?
choices: Cache Genie answers in Dataverse for 24 hours to avoid repeat queries
Always convert Genie results into classic answers before replying
Keep polling the Genie Agent until a response is received, rather than stopping after a few seconds
Never call Genie more than once in a conversation; summarize its first answer instead to keep Copilot Credit costs down
questions.explanation: Genie queries can take longer than a single chat turn. Databricks recommends the instruction 'Always continue polling the Genie Agent until you receive a response. Do not stop after a few seconds.' to avoid repeated 'still processing' messages. Each additional Genie tool call may count as another agent action, so watch credit consumption too.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Besides the Genie tool, what other way does Copilot Studio offer to use Azure Databricks data?
choices: Turn on automatic mirroring of Databricks tables into Dataverse, then ground the agent on the mirrored Dataverse tables
Using Restricted SharePoint Search to index the Databricks catalog
Uploading Delta files directly into Copilot Studio as knowledge documents
Adding Azure Databricks as an advanced knowledge source, choosing a catalog and tables
questions.explanation: Copilot Studio can use Azure Databricks as a knowledge source (Knowledge > + Knowledge > Advanced > Azure Databricks, then pick catalog and tables). The Genie tool path is better for analytical questions because Genie brings its semantic context, instructions and trusted queries rather than raw table access.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: When must the Power Platform Azure Databricks connection use a service principal instead of OAuth?
choices: Whenever Unity Catalog is enabled on the Databricks workspace
When the agent is published to Teams instead of a custom website
When Power Platform and Azure Databricks are in different Microsoft Entra tenants
Whenever the SQL warehouse is serverless, because serverless warehouses don't accept OAuth tokens from Power Platform
questions.explanation: OAuth connections work only if Power Platform and Databricks share an Entra tenant. Otherwise a service principal is required. Coaching angle: a service principal means queries run as that principal, not the end user, so per-user Unity Catalog permissions no longer apply automatically. Prefer same-tenant OAuth for governed analytics.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: What does Databricks list as prerequisites for creating the Azure Databricks connection in Power Platform?
choices: Workspace admin rights plus a Databricks personal access token for every user
A Copilot Studio capacity pack and a Fabric F64 capacity in the same region
A Microsoft 365 E5 license and Purview DSPM for AI enabled in the tenant
An Entra ID account, a premium Power Apps license, and CAN USE on a SQL warehouse
questions.explanation: The setup page lists an Entra ID account, a premium Power Apps license, a Databricks account, and Databricks SQL access with CAN USE on a SQL warehouse. You supply the warehouse's server hostname and HTTP path. The premium Power Apps license is a cost line people often miss.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: Is the Power Platform Azure Databricks connector supported in government clouds?
choices: No. Databricks notes the connector doesn't support government clouds
Yes, but only in GCC High, not in GCC or DoD
Yes, in every sovereign and government cloud
Yes, in GCC and GCC High, as long as the connection uses a service principal instead of OAuth
questions.explanation: Databricks' Copilot Studio page notes the Power Platform connector doesn't support government clouds. For GCC customers, the Copilot Studio-to-Genie path isn't available, so check cloud boundaries before proposing it.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: When connecting a Fabric data agent to Copilot Studio, which authentication choices are offered?
choices: Only service principal authentication through Entra ID
User authentication or agent author authentication
An API key or the workspace's managed identity
Only anonymous access, with the agent's own permissions
questions.explanation: The Fabric data agent connection in Copilot Studio (preview) offers user authentication or agent author authentication. Author auth means every user queries with the author's permissions, an oversharing risk. User auth requires each user to have access to the data agent and its sources.

questions.sectionName: Building and governing Copilot Studio agents
questions.question: A team builds a Copilot Studio agent with a connected Fabric data agent and wants to surface it in Microsoft 365 Copilot. What does Microsoft's documentation say?
choices: It works only after the Fabric data has been mirrored into Dataverse tables
It needs a Fabric F64 or larger capacity before it can appear in Microsoft 365 Copilot
It works in every channel, including Microsoft 365 Copilot, with no extra steps
It isn't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Copilot; Teams is the validated channel
questions.explanation: The Fabric page states that using a custom agent with a connected Fabric data agent isn't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Only Teams is validated, and other channels may work but aren't formally tested. Channel support differs by integration path, so validate the target channel before committing.

questions.question: Which organizational content can Microsoft 365 Copilot surface to a user?
choices: Only content the user created themselves
Anything in the tenant's semantic index, regardless of permissions
Only content the user already has at least view permission to
Only content labeled 'General' or lower
questions.explanation: Copilot surfaces only organizational data the user has at least view permission to, and the semantic index honors that identity-based boundary. Copilot doesn't create new access. It exposes existing oversharing, which is why permission hygiene is step one in any Copilot rollout.

questions.question: Are Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts, responses and Graph data used to train foundation LLMs?
choices: Yes, but only after the data has been anonymized
No. Microsoft states they aren't used to train foundation LLMs
Yes, but only after anonymization, and only for tenants that haven't opted out in the admin center
Only prompts are used for training, never responses
questions.explanation: Microsoft's privacy documentation: prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph aren't used to train foundation LLMs. Feedback data is excluded too. Expect customers to compare this with any other platform's terms.

questions.question: What exception does Microsoft call out to Copilot's EU Data Boundary commitment?
choices: Web search queries are always kept inside the EU
Anthropic models are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary
Copilot Chat (Basic) isn't covered by any residency terms
Copilot in Excel always processes data in US data centers
questions.explanation: Copilot is an EU Data Boundary service: EU traffic stays within the EUDB. Microsoft notes Anthropic models are currently excluded from it. EU customers who let users pick Claude models in Copilot experiences should know their data may be processed outside the boundary.

questions.question: When Copilot uses web search, what is sent outside the Microsoft 365 service boundary?
choices: The full prompt and any attached documents
Generated search queries, sent to Bing
Nothing. Web search runs inside the tenant
The user's mailbox contents
questions.explanation: Web grounding sends generated queries (not the whole prompt) to Bing. Admins can control this with the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy. Regulated customers sometimes disable it.

questions.question: Where are Copilot prompts and responses stored for eDiscovery?
choices: Nowhere. They're discarded after the session
Only in the unified audit log, as event records that eDiscovery can't search directly
In the user's mailbox, findable with a 'Copilot activity' condition
In a Dataverse table created for each tenant
questions.explanation: Copilot interactions are stored in the user's activity history, and Purview eDiscovery finds them in the user's mailbox (filter on Copilot activity). Retention policies apply to prompts and responses, and the unified audit log captures the activity events.

questions.question: A document is encrypted with a sensitivity label. Which usage rights must the user have for Copilot to return its content?
choices: PRINT and EDIT
VIEW only
EXTRACT and VIEW
OWNER
questions.explanation: For encrypted content, users need both EXTRACT and VIEW usage rights for AI apps to return data. That lets customers block AI summarization of specific labeled content without blocking human reading, a precise control worth knowing.

questions.question: What can a Purview DLP policy for Microsoft 365 Copilot do with labeled content?
choices: Prevent Copilot and agents from processing or summarizing items with chosen sensitivity labels
Block users from opening labeled files in the Office desktop apps
Delete labeled files automatically after Copilot has read them once
Automatically relabel sensitive files to 'General' so Copilot can summarize them without exposing the original label
questions.explanation: DLP for Copilot can exclude items with selected sensitivity labels from Copilot and agent processing. At Ignite 2026 Microsoft previewed extending DLP for Copilot to block grounding on sensitive files even when they're unlabeled.

questions.question: Which Insider Risk Management template detects risky AI use such as prompt injection attempts and access to protected materials?
choices: Data theft by departing users
Patient data misuse
Risky AI usage
Security policy violations
questions.explanation: The 'Risky AI usage' policy template in Insider Risk Management detects prompt injection and protected-material access. It pairs with Communication Compliance, which detects policy violations in prompts and responses.

questions.question: What does DSPM for AI's default data risk assessment cover?
choices: It runs weekly on the top 100 SharePoint sites to surface oversharing
It scans every file in the tenant daily for sensitive data and produces a single tenant-wide risk score
It covers only OneDrive accounts of Copilot-licensed users
It covers only sites that already have sensitivity labels
questions.explanation: DSPM for AI runs a default weekly data risk assessment on the top 100 SharePoint sites (custom assessments in preview). First results take about four days. Remediation options include DLP, Restricted Content Discovery, auto-labeling and retention. Microsoft notes the classic DSPM for AI experience has been replaced by a newer DSPM.

questions.question: What does Restricted Content Discovery (RCD) do to a SharePoint site?
choices: Removes every user's permissions on the site except the site owners', so Copilot can no longer see any of its content
Removes the site's content from org-wide search and Copilot discovery without changing permissions
Deletes the site's content from the semantic index permanently
Encrypts every file on the site with a default sensitivity label
questions.explanation: RCD is a site-level setting that hides content from org-wide search (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Copilot discovery, and removes AI entry points on the site. It doesn't change permissions: users with access can still open content directly, and Copilot can still summarize a document a user has open.

questions.question: Which statement about Restricted Content Discovery is true?
choices: It's a permanent security boundary that replaces permission reviews and applies to OneDrive accounts as well as SharePoint sites
It takes effect within seconds, even on sites with millions of items
Microsoft calls it a temporary governance control and warns excessive use reduces Copilot's usefulness
It applies to OneDrive accounts as well as SharePoint sites
questions.explanation: Microsoft positions RCD as temporary. It covers SharePoint sites only (not OneDrive), and propagation can take more than a week for sites with over 500,000 items. Delegating RCD to site admins is off by default and changes need a justification. Fixing permissions is the real remedy.

questions.question: What's the status of Restricted SharePoint Search (RSS) as of late 2026?
choices: It became the default setting for every newly created tenant
Retiring: new enablement is blocked from July 31, 2026, in favor of RCD
It's GA and Microsoft's recommended permanent oversharing control
It was renamed SharePoint Advanced Management and expanded
questions.explanation: RSS let admins limit org-wide search and Copilot to an allow list of up to 100 sites. Microsoft calls it temporary and not a security boundary, and new enablement is blocked starting July 31, 2026. Older readiness playbooks that recommend RSS are out of date.

questions.question: Under Restricted SharePoint Search, which content could users still get in Copilot even if the site wasn't on the allow list?
choices: Content they own, previously accessed, or that was shared with them in Teams or Outlook
Nothing outside the allow list at all, because RSS acts as a hard deny list for Copilot and every other search surface
Any content from sites associated with a hub on the allow list
Only content labeled 'Highly Confidential', which bypasses the list
questions.explanation: RSS isn't a deny list or a security boundary. Users could still reach content they own or recently interacted with, or that was shared with them, even outside the 100-site allow list. Microsoft's deny-style control is SharePoint Advanced Management's Restricted Access Control.

questions.question: Which SharePoint Advanced Management feature restricts a site so only members of specified groups can access it, even if content was shared more broadly?
choices: Restricted SharePoint Search
Inactive site policy
Restricted Access Control (RAC)
Site attestation
questions.explanation: RAC limits site access to specified groups regardless of item-level sharing, which makes it an actual access boundary. SAM's oversharing toolkit also includes data access governance reports (including 'Everyone Except External Users' insights), site access reviews, block download, RCD, and agent access insights.

questions.question: Which SAM report helps find content shared with 'Everyone Except External Users' (EEEU), a common cause of Copilot oversharing?
choices: Microsoft Secure Score
Entra sign-in logs
Copilot Analytics adoption dashboard
Data access governance (DAG) reports
questions.explanation: SAM's data access governance reports include permission state, site permissions, sensitivity label snapshots, sharing link activity and EEEU insights. Site owners can then be asked to fix access through site access reviews.

questions.question: Which governance capabilities does Agent 365 provide for agents in the registry?
choices: Automatically rewriting agent instructions to strip out sensitive terms and names
Pre-publish review and approval, finding ownerless agents, and tool connection controls
Converting third-party agents into Copilot Studio agents for central management
Training custom models on agent conversations to improve answer quality
questions.explanation: Agent 365 governance includes pre-publish review and approval, ownerless-agent detection and reassignment, tool connection controls, policy templates and a Purview activity record. Security adds risk signals from Defender, Entra and Purview, with the ability to block agents. Business value includes Copilot Credits cost management with spending limits.

questions.question: What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID?
choices: A standard user account created for each employee who builds an agent
A Purview sensitivity label applied automatically to agent-generated content
A license key assigned to each Copilot Studio agent so it can be published to Teams and appear in the Agent Store
Dedicated identities for AI agents, created from blueprints, supporting OAuth, MCP and A2A
questions.explanation: Entra Agent ID extends Entra capabilities to AI agents with a dedicated agent identity type, blueprints (templates with parent-child relationships) for consistent policy at scale, and support for OAuth 2.0, MCP and A2A. All agent authentication and activity is logged. Extending Entra security features to agents requires Agent 365.

questions.question: How can non-Microsoft agents (for example on AWS Bedrock or n8n) get Entra agent identities?
choices: By assigning each one a Microsoft 365 Copilot license
Only by rebuilding and hosting them in Microsoft Foundry
Through the Entra ID Auth SDK (sidecar) or workload identity federation
They can't. Agent ID covers only agents built in Copilot Studio and Foundry inside the same tenant
questions.explanation: Entra Agent ID integrates non-Microsoft agents through the Entra ID Auth SDK sidecar or workload identity federation. A Databricks-hosted agent can, in principle, be governed under the same identity umbrella. Governance doesn't force a single-vendor agent strategy.

questions.question: Where are Copilot prompts and responses captured for audit?
choices: Copilot interactions aren't audited
In the Microsoft Purview unified audit log
Only in each user's browser history
In Azure Monitor Logs only
questions.explanation: Purview captures Copilot prompts and responses in the unified audit log, which feeds investigations, Communication Compliance and Insider Risk. Customers comparing platforms should ask where each agent's conversations are audited. Genie, for example, exports traces and logs MCP connector activity on the Databricks side.

questions.question: What does Microsoft say about the data terms for third-party agents used inside Copilot?
choices: They're blocked in every tenant until Microsoft certifies them
They may only use public web data, never organizational content
They automatically inherit Microsoft's Product Terms and Data Protection Addendum
Third-party agents have their own terms, and admins choose which agents are allowed
questions.explanation: Microsoft's privacy page notes third-party agents carry their own terms. Admins decide which are allowed. When a customer brings Genie into Copilot, review both Databricks' and Microsoft's terms and data flows, for example the Teams app's central service location.

questions.question: What caveat does Microsoft note about encryption and content accessed through agents?
choices: Encryption is removed automatically whenever an agent reads a protected file, so agents always see the full content
Encryption can exclude programmatic access, so agents may not see some encrypted content
Agents bypass encryption whenever the requesting user is the file's owner
Encrypted content is always fully available to every agent in the tenant
questions.explanation: Microsoft's privacy guidance warns that encryption can exclude programmatic access for content accessed through agents. Heavily encrypted repositories may produce incomplete agent answers, which is a usability tradeoff of strong protection.

questions.question: Can Copilot read a password-protected document the user hasn't opened?
choices: Only if the file is stored in the user's own OneDrive
Yes, because the semantic index has already processed it
No. Password-protected documents aren't accessible to AI apps unless already open
Yes, as long as the user has view permission, because the semantic index stores the file's text before it's protected
questions.explanation: Purview's AI documentation notes password-protected documents aren't accessible to AI apps unless already open, and S/MIME-encrypted email isn't returned by Copilot. Users sometimes interpret these as Copilot 'missing' content.

questions.question: What happens if an admin turns off 'connected experiences that analyze content' to tighten privacy?
choices: Copilot keeps working everywhere but stops citing its sources
Nothing; Copilot is exempt from connected-experience settings
Only Copilot Chat on the web is affected; in-app Copilot keeps working
Copilot features in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote are removed
questions.explanation: Microsoft notes that disabling connected experiences that analyze content removes Copilot features in the Office apps. It's a blunt switch, and a customer using it for privacy reasons effectively turns off in-app Copilot.

questions.question: What identity do Foundry hosted agents get?
choices: A dedicated Microsoft Entra identity
A shared tenant-wide service account
No identity; they authenticate with API keys only
They borrow the identity of whichever user is chatting
questions.explanation: Foundry hosted agents get a dedicated Entra identity, and prompt agents also use Entra agent identities. MCP tools in Foundry support key-based auth, Entra (agent or project managed identity), OAuth on-behalf-of, or unauthenticated. Choose OBO when downstream data (like Genie over Unity Catalog) must enforce per-user permissions.

questions.question: What did Microsoft announce at Ignite 2026 for Purview DLP and Copilot?
choices: Retirement of DLP for Copilot in favor of Restricted Content Discovery
Automatic deletion of overshared files that DSPM for AI has flagged
General availability of DLP for Copilot, limited to Excel workbooks
A preview that blocks grounding on sensitive files even when they're unlabeled
questions.explanation: The Book of News lists DLP for Copilot extensions in preview: blocking grounding on sensitive files even when unlabeled, and extending prompt protection to attachments. Until it's generally available, customers with incomplete labeling should keep relying on permissions, labels and RCD.

questions.question: What did Microsoft announce at Ignite 2026 to protect local agents such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot CLI on endpoints?
choices: Defender runtime protection for local agents (requiring Defender for Endpoint P2)
Automatic migration of local agents into Copilot Studio environments
A new Windows edition that blocks any unsigned agent from running
A tenant-wide ban on running local agents on any device used by a Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed user
questions.explanation: Ignite 2026 extended Defender runtime protection to local agents, requiring Defender for Endpoint P2, alongside Entra Agent ID for discovered local agents (preview) and Intune governance previews. Microsoft is building a cross-vendor agent security story, which a multi-platform customer can use.

questions.question: Why does Microsoft describe Restricted SharePoint Search as not a security boundary?
choices: Because it applies only to files shared in Teams chats
Because it encrypts the content of excluded sites instead of hiding it from search and Copilot
Because it only applies to external and guest users
It doesn't change permissions; people with access can still reach content
questions.explanation: RSS, like RCD, hides content from discovery without changing permissions. Anyone with access can still reach content directly. Real boundaries come from permissions, RAC, sensitivity labels with encryption, and DLP.

questions.question: What does Agent 365 offer for agent cost governance?
choices: Cost tracking for the Azure VMs that host agents only
Copilot Credits cost management with spending limits per user or group
Automatic refunds for agent runs that fail or time out
A fixed monthly price per agent that includes unlimited usage, so agent costs never vary
questions.explanation: Agent 365's business value pillar includes Copilot Credits cost management with spending limits per user and group. At Ignite 2026 Microsoft added cost management, forecasting and recommendations, in preview or Frontier stages.

questions.question: Which SharePoint Advanced Management capability lets an organization delegate permission clean-up to site owners at scale?
choices: Copilot Notebooks
Restricted SharePoint Search
Customer Lockbox
Site access reviews
questions.explanation: Site access reviews, driven from DAG reports, ask site owners to review and fix sharing. That scales oversharing remediation beyond central IT, which is usually the critical path for a broad Copilot rollout.

questions.question: Which Agent 365 governance feature addresses agents whose creators have left the company?
choices: Finding agents without an owner and assigning one
Converting the agent into a SharePoint page
Transferring the agent's credits to the user's manager
Automatic deletion of all agents older than 90 days
questions.explanation: Agent 365 surfaces ownerless agents so admins can assign an accountable owner. Sprawl and orphaned agents with live data connections are a major governance risk, whatever platform built them.

questions.question: What is the release status of Microsoft Fabric data agents as of late 2026?
choices: Public preview with no SLA
Retired in favor of Copilot Studio
Generally available
Private preview only
questions.explanation: Microsoft's concept page describes the Fabric data agent as a generally available feature for building conversational Q&A over Fabric data with generative AI. Some consumption paths (such as Copilot Studio connected agents) are still labeled preview.

questions.question: How many data sources can a single Fabric data agent use?
choices: Up to five, mixing lakehouses, warehouses, KQL, semantic models, ontologies and Graph
Exactly one data source per agent, chosen when the agent is created, though that source can be a lakehouse or warehouse
Up to 50 tables, drawn from any number of lakehouses or warehouses
Unlimited sources, as long as they all live in the same workspace
questions.explanation: Fabric data agents support up to five data sources in any combination: lakehouses, warehouses, KQL databases, Power BI semantic models, ontologies and Microsoft Graph, plus mirrored databases. For comparison, Databricks raised Genie Agents to 50 tables, views or metric views per agent in 2026.

questions.question: What is the maximum size of a result a Fabric data agent will return?
choices: 10,000 rows with no column limit
25 rows and 25 columns
The full query result, streamed in pages
1,000 rows and 100 columns
questions.explanation: Fabric data agent responses are capped at a maximum of 25 rows and 25 columns. It's built for answers, not extracts. If a business user expects a detailed list, set expectations or use a report or a Genie Agent instead.

questions.question: Which of these is a documented limitation of Fabric data agents?
choices: They can write results back to source tables when users ask them to
They require a separate Azure OpenAI resource to be deployed for each agent
No unstructured data (PDF, DOCX, TXT), English only, and the LLM can't be changed
They can only query Power BI semantic models, not lakehouses or warehouses
questions.explanation: Limitations include no unstructured files, lakehouse files must be exposed as tables, English only, a fixed LLM, and strictly read-only queries (SQL, DAX, KQL). Example queries are allowed (up to 100 per source) but not for semantic model sources.

questions.question: A Fabric data agent's capacity is in West Europe but one of its lakehouse sources is on a capacity in East US. What happens?
choices: It fails; the source's capacity must be in the same region as the agent's
It works, but only after cross-geo processing for AI is enabled
It works, but every query runs more slowly across the two regions
Fabric automatically mirrors the lakehouse into West Europe first
questions.explanation: Microsoft's limitations say the agent fails if a data source's capacity is in a different region from the agent's capacity. Multi-region data estates need careful placement, unlike federated query approaches.

questions.question: What Fabric capacity does a data agent require?
choices: Any capacity at all, including a Fabric trial capacity
No capacity, because data agents run serverless in Azure
A paid F2+ Fabric capacity, or Power BI Premium P1+, with Fabric enabled
An F64 or larger Fabric capacity; smaller F SKUs and Premium P1 capacities can't host data agents
questions.explanation: The prerequisite is a paid F2+ capacity or P1+ with Fabric enabled, plus the tenant setting for cross-geo processing and storing for AI. The F64 minimum for Copilot and AI features was dropped to F2 in 2025, but small capacities can throttle under agent load.

questions.question: Which tenant setting does Microsoft list as a prerequisite for Fabric data agents?
choices: Allow external sharing of Fabric items with anyone
Enable cross-geo processing and cross-geo storing for AI
Disable Microsoft Graph grounding for all Copilot users
Enable Restricted SharePoint Search for the tenant
questions.explanation: Fabric data agents require the admin setting that allows cross-geo processing and storing for AI. For customers with strict residency requirements, this is a decision point, and the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio integration pages also warn responses may be processed outside Fabric's compliance boundary.

questions.question: Whose permissions does a Fabric data agent use when it queries data?
choices: Fabric administrator permissions, filtered by sensitivity labels
A workspace managed identity that has full read access to sources
The agent creator's identity, so everyone using a shared agent sees exactly what the creator can see in each source
The requesting user's identity and permissions; RLS and CLS on semantic models still apply
questions.explanation: Fabric data agents access sources with the requesting user's identity. Sharing an agent doesn't grant access to its sources. For semantic models, Read permission is needed (Build isn't), and row- and column-level security still apply. That's the same principle as Genie with Unity Catalog: the agent shouldn't widen access.

questions.question: How are Copilot and data agent tokens metered against Fabric capacity?
choices: A flat 1 CU second per question, regardless of how many tokens are used
They aren't metered at all, because Copilot in Fabric is free on F2 and up
1 Copilot Credit per 1,000 tokens, billed to the tenant's Azure subscription rather than to any Fabric capacity at all
100 CU seconds per 1,000 input tokens, 10 per 1,000 cached input tokens, and 400 per 1,000 output tokens
questions.explanation: Copilot in Fabric rates: input 100, cached input 10, output 400 CU seconds per 1,000 tokens, applied across Copilot experiences including data agents. Microsoft's example: 2,000 input + 500 output tokens is 400 CU seconds per request. It runs as a background job, which smooths throttling. Fabric agents spend Fabric CUs, not Copilot Credits.

questions.question: What does a Fabric Copilot capacity do?
choices: Provides a separate, free capacity reserved for Copilot features so that AI usage never counts against paid capacities
Hosts Microsoft 365 Copilot inside Fabric for users without licenses
Bills chosen users' Copilot and data agent usage to one capacity, not the content's
Doubles the CU limit of every capacity during business hours for AI
questions.explanation: By default Copilot usage bills to the capacity holding the user's content. A Fabric Copilot capacity (minimum F2 or P1, home region only) lets admins send a group of users' Copilot and data agent usage to one capacity, which centralizes chargeback and protects production capacities from AI spikes.

questions.question: A user is assigned to two Fabric Copilot capacities. Which one is billed?
choices: Both capacities are billed, with usage split evenly between them until an admin removes one of the assignments
Whichever of the two capacities has the larger SKU
The most recently created one; each user effectively has one Copilot capacity
The one in the same region as the content being queried
questions.explanation: Microsoft's rules: an assigned Copilot capacity takes precedence over the workspace capacity, each user has one Copilot capacity, and if several apply, the most recently created wins. Embedded license mode and Fabric AI functions aren't supported.

questions.question: How do users consume a published Fabric data agent from Microsoft 365 Copilot or Teams?
choices: Add the agent's lakehouse to Microsoft 365 as a Copilot connector
Publish the agent (optionally to the Agent Store) and @-mention it in Teams or Copilot Chat
Embed it in a Power BI report, which is the only supported surface
Export the agent as a Copilot Studio solution file and import it there, because Fabric agents can't be published directly
questions.explanation: After publishing, optionally with 'Publish to Agent Store', users can use the data agent in Teams or Copilot Chat with @. Microsoft notes responses may be processed outside Fabric's compliance boundary, and sharing requires recipients to have access to the agent and all its sources.

questions.question: When you mirror an Azure Databricks Unity Catalog catalog into Fabric, what is actually copied?
choices: A full copy of every Delta table is written into OneLake as new Parquet files, then refreshed on a schedule
Only the Power BI semantic models that were built on Databricks data
Only the catalog structure (metadata); data is read in place through OneLake shortcuts
Nothing; mirroring just adds a link to the Databricks workspace UI
questions.explanation: Fabric mirrors only the Azure Databricks catalog structure, and the data is accessed through shortcuts. Fabric creates a mirrored item and an autogenerated SQL analytics endpoint. Schema changes can take seconds to minutes to appear.

questions.question: Which Unity Catalog tables does Microsoft list as not supported for mirroring into Fabric?
choices: Tables with row-level security or column masking policies, plus views and shared tables
Any table larger than 1 TB, because shortcuts can't handle that size
Managed tables, because only external tables in customer-owned storage can be mirrored into Fabric through shortcuts
Tables that use liquid clustering, deletion vectors or column mapping
questions.explanation: Fabric's limitations list tables with RLS and column-masking policies as unsupported, along with views, metric views, lakehouse federated tables and Delta Sharing tables. The best-governed tables, the ones with row filters and masks, are exactly the ones that don't come across. Genie queries them in place with Unity Catalog enforcing policies per user.

questions.question: What networking prerequisite applies to mirroring an Azure Databricks catalog into Fabric?
choices: Fabric must be deployed into the customer's own virtual network first
The workspace must use only a Databricks-managed storage account
The Databricks workspace must have public network access fully disabled before Fabric is allowed to mirror its catalog
The ADLS Gen2 storage account behind the Databricks workspace must also be accessible to Fabric
questions.explanation: Because mirrored data is read via shortcuts, Fabric needs access to the underlying ADLS Gen2 account. That opens a second access path to the data outside Unity Catalog's control, so it should be reviewed by the security team.

questions.question: Do Unity Catalog views and metric views appear in a mirrored Azure Databricks item in Fabric?
choices: Yes, as Power BI measures
No. Views and metric views aren't mirrored
Yes, as Fabric warehouse views
Only metric views are mirrored
questions.explanation: Metadata sync covers schema and table changes, but views and metric views don't appear. The semantic layer a customer built in Unity Catalog (metric views, business logic in views) doesn't carry into Fabric. Genie uses those assets directly.

questions.question: What does Foundry Agent Service charge for a prompt agent?
choices: Nothing; prompt agents are free
Per-call model inference plus tool usage
A flat monthly fee per agent
Copilot Credits at 5 per action
questions.explanation: Foundry's cost model: prompt agents bill per-call inference plus tool usage; hosted agents add container compute; voice agents bill Voice Live and model usage. Agent Service pricing details live on a separate Azure pricing page. A Foundry agent published into Microsoft 365 still incurs these Azure costs.

questions.question: Which MCP authentication options does Foundry Agent Service support for tools?
choices: Key-based, Entra (agent or project managed identity), OAuth on-behalf-of, or unauthenticated
Only API keys, which must be stored in an Azure Key Vault inside the Foundry project and rotated every 90 days
Only user passwords, which the agent collects once at sign-in
Only the Foundry project's system-assigned managed identity, nothing else
questions.explanation: Foundry supports multiple MCP auth modes. When connecting a Foundry agent to Databricks' managed MCP server for Genie, OAuth on-behalf-of keeps Unity Catalog enforcement per user. A managed identity would query as the agent, which is a different governance posture.

questions.question: Which tools does the Foundry overview list as available to agents?
choices: Only tools that were first built and published in Copilot Studio
Only Bing search and Azure SQL Database queries; MCP and OpenAPI tools must be built in Copilot Studio and imported
Web search, file search, code interpreter, memory, functions, OpenAPI specs and MCP servers
Only Microsoft Graph, through the Work IQ API with Copilot Credits
questions.explanation: Foundry agents can use web search, file search, code interpreter, memory, functions, OpenAPI tools and MCP servers. Hosted agents also get SharePoint, Work IQ and Fabric IQ. MCP is the open path for connecting Genie or any other enterprise system.

questions.question: Does configuring or sharing a Fabric data agent grant users access to its underlying data?
choices: Yes. Sharing the agent grants read access to all sources
Only if the agent is published to the Agent Store
No. Users still need their own access to the sources
Yes, but only for semantic model sources
questions.explanation: Microsoft is explicit that configuring or sharing a data agent doesn't grant access to its sources. Rollout plans need both agent sharing and data access provisioning, the same pattern as Genie Agents, which answer only from data the user can access.

questions.question: What does Microsoft warn about responses from a Fabric data agent used in Microsoft 365 Copilot?
choices: Responses are only visible to Fabric administrators
Responses are cached in a public CDN for 24 hours so that repeated questions from other users load faster
Responses may be processed outside Fabric's compliance boundary or geographic region
Responses can't include numbers or calculated values
questions.explanation: The Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio integration pages both warn that responses may be sent outside Fabric's compliance boundary or region. Residency-sensitive customers should treat every cross-product AI hop, Fabric to Copilot or Databricks to Copilot, as a data flow to document.

questions.question: What permission on a Power BI semantic model does a user need to query it through a Fabric data agent?
choices: Read permission on the model; workspace access and Build aren't required
Workspace Admin role on the model's workspace
The Fabric Administrator role for the tenant
Build permission on the model plus the Contributor role on its workspace, since data agents generate DAX
questions.explanation: For semantic model sources, Read permission is needed, not workspace access, and Build isn't required. RLS and CLS still apply. That makes it practical to expose governed models to many consumers.

questions.question: What are the three members of Databricks' Genie family as of late 2026, and who is each for?
choices: Genie One for business users, Genie Agents for data teams, Genie Code for developers
Genie for Teams, Genie for Excel and Genie for Power BI users
Genie Free, Genie Pro and Genie Enterprise, priced per seat tier
Genie Chat for analysts, Genie Spaces for dashboards and Genie Notebooks for data engineers, priced per seat
questions.explanation: Databricks describes Genie as a family of AI data experiences: Genie One (an agentic coworker for business users), Genie Agents (curated domain agents built by data teams) and Genie Code (for developers). Databricks says all three are generally available.

questions.question: What were Genie Agents called before mid-2026?
choices: Lakeview apps
Genie spaces
AI/BI dashboards
Databricks Assistants
questions.explanation: Databricks renamed Genie spaces to Genie Agents in July 2026, with capabilities unchanged. Microsoft-side documentation now asks for a 'Genie Agent ID' when configuring the Copilot Studio tool. Expect older customer material to still say 'space'.

questions.question: What is Genie Ontology?
choices: A Power BI semantic model export format that Genie reads on startup
A manual business glossary that admins must write and approve before Genie will answer any question in a workspace
An automatic context layer behind Genie One and Genie Agents that maps business meaning
A licensing tier that unlocks Genie for more than 100 users
questions.explanation: Databricks introduced Genie Ontology in June 2026 as an automatic context layer. It weighs sources by authority, usage and ties to certified assets, and shows users only content they're permitted to see. It's in public preview and can take external knowledge such as Power BI files (beta).

questions.question: How does Databricks price Genie One and Genie Agents for end users?
choices: No seats: a monthly free AI allowance per user, then usage, with compute billed separately
$30 per user per month, matching Microsoft 365 Copilot, with SQL warehouse compute included in the seat price
Only SQL warehouse compute; Genie never charges anything for LLM usage
A flat per-workspace fee that includes unlimited users and compute
questions.explanation: Databricks says Genie has no seat-based pricing: users get $10 of free usage per month (150 DBUs, which is $10.50 in US East), then pay for AI used beyond that. The free allowance covers Genie LLM usage only, and compute (for example serverless SQL) is billed separately. Compare that with Copilot's $30 seat plus credits.

questions.question: What did Databricks announce in July 2026 about billing for Genie One and Genie Agents?
choices: Genie One became permanently free for all Azure Databricks customers, including the SQL compute behind each answer
Billing doubled for users who don't hold a Databricks SQL license
Usage is free through January 31, 2027, with prior charges negated by correction records
Billing moved to a flat per-question fee of $0.10 for every user
questions.explanation: Databricks paused Genie One and Genie Agents billing and said usage is free through January 31, 2027. Correction records in system.billing.usage negate prior billed usage, and budgets net them out. Genie Code is unaffected. Underlying compute is still billed, so customers should plan for post-January 2027 pricing.

questions.question: A customer runs Genie through a service principal for a shared Copilot Studio agent. How is that usage billed?
choices: Free, because service principals are treated as system identities
Standard pay-as-you-go: service principals don't get the per-user free usage
At double the normal user rate, as a deterrent to shared identities
It's blocked, because service principals can't call Genie at all
questions.explanation: Databricks' September 2026 change: service principals are excluded from free usage and billed at standard PAYG. A service principal also weakens per-user Unity Catalog enforcement, so this is a cost and a governance reason to prefer per-user OAuth (OBO) integrations.

questions.question: How does Genie enforce data access in its answers?
choices: Genie applies the Genie Agent author's permissions for everyone who asks, so sharing an agent shares the author's access
Genie doesn't enforce permissions; the warehouse owner's access applies
Genie relies on Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to filter answers
Unity Catalog or source ACLs are enforced on every answer, using the asker's identity
questions.explanation: Databricks says permissions are enforced by default on every answer through source-native ACLs or Unity Catalog, and answers come only from sources the user can access. In the Teams app, each request runs with the asking user's permissions. Unity Catalog row filters and column masks stay in force because data is queried in place.

questions.question: What caveat does Databricks note about Genie One artifacts?
choices: Artifacts expire automatically 15 minutes after they're created
Artifacts re-run their queries for each viewer using that viewer's own permissions, so sharing them is always safe
Artifacts store a data snapshot, so any viewer sees that data without source access
Artifacts can only be viewed by workspace admins and their creator
questions.explanation: Per the November 2026 release notes, artifacts snapshot their data, so sharing an artifact shares the data regardless of source permissions. It's the Genie equivalent of emailing a spreadsheet. Governance coaching should cover artifact sharing.

questions.question: Which Genie integration does the Azure Databricks Microsoft 365 Copilot page label as recommended?
choices: A Copilot connector that crawls Databricks tables into the index
Exporting Genie results to SharePoint for Copilot to index
Mirroring Unity Catalog into Fabric and publishing a Fabric data agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot
The Azure Databricks Genie plugin for Copilot Chat and Cowork (public preview)
questions.explanation: The M365 Copilot page lists three options: (1) the Azure Databricks Genie plugin, recommended and in public preview, for Copilot Chat and Cowork, answering via Genie One; (2) the Databricks Genie app in Teams, used from Copilot with @-mention; (3) Copilot Studio, connecting to individual Genie Agents.

questions.question: What does the Azure Databricks Genie plugin require on the Microsoft side?
choices: A Fabric F2 capacity
Only a Copilot Chat (Basic) entitlement
A Copilot Studio capacity pack
A Microsoft 365 Copilot license
questions.explanation: The plugin path (Copilot Chat and Cowork) requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and a workspace with Genie One enabled. Users install it from Plugins, enter the server hostname, and sign in with Entra ID. For unlicensed users, the Teams app is the path to consider.

questions.question: Which limitations does Databricks list for the Genie plugin in Copilot Chat and Cowork?
choices: It's limited to 10 users per tenant during public preview, and it needs a service principal instead of Entra ID sign-in
Workspace-level Genie One only, no VNet support, and one non-shareable connection per user
English only, with all results returned as downloadable CSV files
A maximum of 10 users per tenant while the plugin is in public preview
questions.explanation: The plugin supports workspace-level Genie One only, has no VNet support, and each user creates their own connection, which can't be shared. Customers with locked-down network architectures should check the no-VNet constraint early.

questions.question: What's the key scope difference between the Copilot Studio path and the plugin or Teams app paths for Genie?
choices: Copilot Studio can query Delta tables without Genie
There is no difference; all paths use the same Genie One endpoint
Copilot Studio connects to individual Genie Agents only, not Genie One
Copilot Studio connects to Genie One only, not Genie Agents
questions.explanation: The Copilot Studio tool targets a specific Genie Agent by ID. The plugin and Teams app answer through Genie One (or a pinned Genie Agent in Teams). Copilot Studio suits a curated, domain-specific experience. Genie One suits broad 'ask anything' access.

questions.question: How do users invoke Databricks Genie from Microsoft 365 Copilot when the Genie app for Teams is installed?
choices: @-mention 'Azure Databricks Genie' in Copilot Chat or select it under Agents
Users must leave Copilot and open a Databricks browser tab
Copilot routes every data question to Genie automatically, no mention needed
Through a SharePoint page that embeds the Genie experience
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot sends a question to Genie only when you @-mention it or chat with it directly. Copilot doesn't route data questions to Genie on its own, so user enablement matters. The plugin path doesn't need an @-mention.

questions.question: Where does the central service behind the Databricks Genie app for Teams run, and what does it store?
choices: In Microsoft's Teams data center, storing query results for 30 days
In East US 2 regardless of workspace region, storing only the tenant-to-workspace mapping
In the same region as each workspace, storing the full conversation history and query results for 30 days
In the customer's own Azure subscription, storing nothing at all
questions.explanation: The Teams app's central service runs in East US 2 whatever the workspace region and stores only the tenant-to-workspace mapping. LLM processing follows the workspace's Geo and cross-Geo setting. Workspaces with IP access lists must allow the East US 2 control-plane outbound IPs.

questions.question: Users see 'Need admin approval' when signing in to the Databricks Genie app in Teams. What's the fix?
choices: Turn on the Managed MCP Servers preview in the workspace
Grant tenant-wide admin consent for the Azure Databricks enterprise application
Assign every Teams user a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, because the Genie app only signs in licensed users
Add the users to the Copilot Studio authors security group
questions.explanation: This error means tenant-wide admin consent is missing for the Azure Databricks enterprise app in Entra ID. A Microsoft 365 admin must also install 'Databricks Genie' from the Microsoft marketplace and approve its permissions. It's a common rollout blocker, so bring the Entra admin in early.

questions.question: A customer's workspace uses Azure Private Link. What does the Genie Teams app need?
choices: An account admin adds a context-based ingress rule for the Genie Teams app
A Copilot Studio VNet gateway must be deployed in the workspace
Nothing, because Microsoft Teams supports outbound Private Link to Azure Databricks workspaces natively
The workspace must be switched back to public network access
questions.explanation: Teams doesn't support outbound Private Link, so an account admin must add a context-based ingress rule (API, Genie scope, source Partner Platforms > Databricks Teams App). The policy can take up to 30 minutes to take effect.

questions.question: Can users pick which SQL warehouse the Genie Teams app uses?
choices: No. Azure Databricks automatically selects a SQL warehouse the user is authorized to access
No. It always uses a dedicated Teams warehouse billed to Microsoft
Yes, but only workspace admins can choose it for everyone
Yes. Each user picks a warehouse from a dropdown at the start of a chat, and admins can pin a default per channel
questions.explanation: The Teams app auto-selects a warehouse the user can access. For cost governance, use warehouse permissions and budgets so Teams usage lands on an appropriately sized serverless warehouse.

questions.question: What file-upload limits apply in the Genie Teams app?
choices: Any chat or channel, with unlimited uploads of up to 1 GB per file, including in Microsoft 365 Copilot
Channels only, one file at a time, in any format up to 100 MiB
File uploads aren't supported in the Genie Teams app at all
DMs only, without a pinned agent: up to five PDF, DOCX or CSV files, 20 MiB each
questions.explanation: Uploads work in DMs without a pinned agent: up to five PDF, DOCX or CSV files, each 20 MiB or less. They aren't available in channels, group chats or Microsoft 365 Copilot, and OneDrive for Business is required.

questions.question: How does Copilot Cowork reach Databricks data?
choices: Through the Genie plugin, which reaches Genie One via the Genie managed MCP server
It can't; Cowork has no way to reach Databricks data today
By crawling Unity Catalog tables into the Microsoft 365 semantic index overnight, so Cowork can answer without Databricks
Only through Fabric mirroring, with a Fabric data agent in between
questions.explanation: The Cowork page describes connecting Copilot Cowork to Genie One through the Azure Databricks Genie plugin (public preview), using the Genie managed MCP server. When a Cowork task needs data (say a Q3 revenue deck), Cowork calls Genie One, and answers come with progress updates, visuals and citations. Cowork requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

questions.question: When a Cowork task calls Genie One through the plugin, which two meters run?
choices: Only Copilot Credits; Databricks waives all charges for Cowork calls
Neither, because plugin calls are free on both sides by agreement
Copilot Credits for Cowork's tool calls, plus Databricks usage (AI and compute)
Only Databricks DBUs; Microsoft waives Cowork charges for plugin calls
questions.explanation: Cowork bills model responses and tool or skill calls in Copilot Credits, and Genie runs on Databricks compute with its own AI usage model (currently free through January 2027, compute still billed). Model both sides, and don't assume Copilot 'includes' the data platform.

questions.question: What is the URL pattern for a Genie Agent's Databricks managed MCP server?
choices: https://<workspace-hostname>/genie/mcp/v1/{agent_name}
https://<workspace-hostname>/api/2.0/mcp/genie/{genie_space_id}
https://<workspace-hostname>/api/2.0/sql/statements/genie
https://mcp.databricks.com/{tenant_id}/genie
questions.explanation: Databricks' managed MCP server for a Genie Agent uses /api/2.0/mcp/genie/{genie_space_id} with the 'genie' OAuth scope. It's public preview and needs the 'Managed MCP Servers' preview enabled by a workspace admin. The Genie One MCP is GA. Any MCP-capable agent (Copilot Studio, Foundry and others) can use these endpoints.

questions.question: What must a workspace admin enable before Copilot Studio can use the Azure Databricks Genie tool?
choices: The 'Managed MCP Servers' preview on the workspace Previews page
Lakehouse Federation for Unity Catalog
Delta Sharing to the Microsoft tenant
Serverless notebooks and jobs, which the Copilot Studio connector uses to run Genie queries
questions.explanation: Both the Copilot Studio page and the managed MCP docs require the 'Managed MCP Servers' preview. Because it's a preview, confirm that the customer's policy allows preview features in production, or plan for it.

questions.question: How many tables, views or metric views can a Genie Agent include after Databricks' September 2026 update?
choices: Up to 50 (up from 30)
Up to 5
Up to 25
Unlimited
questions.explanation: In September 2026 Databricks raised the limit to 50 tables, views or metric views per agent (from 30) and up to 200,000 conversations per agent (from 10,000). Compare Fabric data agents' five data sources and 25×25 result cap.

questions.question: What does 'account-only user access to Genie One' (beta, September 2026) allow?
choices: Registered-IdP users can use account-level Genie One without workspace assignment
Users can reach Genie One only through Microsoft 365 Copilot
Anonymous guests can use Genie One without signing in, as long as the workspace allows public access
Only account admins can use Genie One at the account level
questions.explanation: This beta lets users in a registered IdP reach account-level Genie One without being assigned to a workspace or given consumer access, which simplifies broad rollout to business users. Note that the Copilot plugin currently supports workspace-level Genie One only.

questions.question: What does Databricks' 'consumer access' entitlement grant?
choices: Full workspace admin rights, scoped down to Genie and dashboards
A Microsoft 365 Copilot license for using Genie from Teams
Read access to every Unity Catalog table in the workspace's metastore, so business users can query anything they find
Business users access to consumption experiences without granting any additional data permissions
questions.explanation: Consumer access lets business users use Genie and other consumer experiences, and Databricks notes it doesn't grant additional permissions. Data access still comes from Unity Catalog grants. Some features (file upload in Genie One, web_search and sandbox MCPs) aren't available to consumer-only users.

questions.question: In Databricks' June 2026 internal benchmark of 28 real-world questions, how did Genie compare with the strongest general-purpose coding agent tested?
choices: Genie answered 52.4% correctly versus 84.5% for the coding agent
Genie answered 99% correctly versus 25% for the coding agent
Both answered about 70% correctly on the first attempt
Genie answered 84.5% correctly on the first attempt versus 52.4%
questions.explanation: Databricks reported 84.5% first-attempt accuracy for Genie versus 52.4% for the strongest general-purpose agent (25% for the weakest), with competitors anonymized. It's a vendor benchmark, so use it as a prompt for the customer to run their own head-to-head on their data. Genie supports benchmarks to do exactly that.

questions.question: Databricks also ships an MCP connector so Genie One can reach Microsoft 365 content. What does it cover and how do users authenticate?
choices: SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Outlook and Calendar via Graph, each user signing in
Only Teams messages, with no user authentication required
Only SharePoint, through a shared service account set up by an admin
All Microsoft 365 data, read through a single tenant admin's delegated token configured once by the workspace admin
questions.explanation: The integration goes both ways: Genie into Copilot, and Microsoft 365 into Genie One. Databricks' Microsoft 365 connector reaches SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Outlook and Calendar through Graph, and each user authenticates individually, so Microsoft 365 permissions are respected. Genie One can then combine Microsoft 365 context with governed lakehouse data.

questions.question: In the Genie Teams app, an admin pins a Genie Agent. What happens to existing Genie One conversations?
choices: They're deleted when the new agent is pinned
They become read-only for 30 days, then archived
They're migrated to the newly pinned agent, so users pick up where they left off with the new agent's context
They stay on Genie One; only new conversations go to the pinned agent
questions.explanation: Pinning affects only new conversations; existing ones stay on Genie One. Settings changes can take up to an hour. Expect to explain this to users after a configuration change.

questions.question: A 20,000-person customer is licensing Microsoft 365 Copilot for only 3,000 people but wants governed self-service analytics for everyone. Which documented Genie path doesn't depend on a Microsoft 365 Copilot license?
choices: @-mentioning Genie inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, which every Teams user can do without a Copilot license
The Genie plugin used from inside Copilot Cowork tasks
The Azure Databricks Genie plugin installed in Copilot Chat
Chatting with the Databricks Genie app directly in Microsoft Teams
questions.explanation: Databricks lists a Microsoft 365 Copilot license as a requirement for the plugin and Cowork paths. The Genie app in Teams is installed by a Microsoft 365 admin and used in Teams chats with each user's own Entra identity. That puts governed analytics in front of all 20,000 people, with Copilot-licensed users also able to @-mention Genie from Copilot.

questions.question: A Copilot Studio agent grounded on SharePoint is offered to 15,000 users without Copilot licenses in Copilot Chat. Each asks 10 grounded questions a month. Using standard rates, what's the monthly PAYG cost?
choices: About $18,000: 15,000 × 10 × 12 credits = 1.8M credits at $0.01
$0, because Copilot Chat agents are free for E5 users
About $1,500: 15,000 × 10 × 1 credit per classic answer
About $450,000: 15,000 users × $30, since agent usage requires a Copilot seat for each user
questions.explanation: Each grounded answer is 2 (generative answer) + 10 (tenant graph grounding) = 12 credits. 150,000 questions × 12 = 1.8M credits, which is $18,000 a month at PAYG list, or about 72 capacity packs ($14,400) if usage is steady. Grounding is 83% of this bill. Narrowing knowledge scope or licensing the heaviest users changes the math.

questions.question: At PAYG list price, roughly how many tenant-grounded agent prompts (12 credits each) per month make an unlicensed user's metered agent usage cost about the same as a $30 Copilot seat?
choices: About 250 prompts a month (3,000 credits)
About 2,500 prompts a month (30,000 credits)
About 25 prompts a month (300 credits)
Never. Metered usage is always cheaper than a seat
questions.explanation: $30 ÷ $0.01 = 3,000 credits, and 3,000 ÷ 12 is about 250 grounded prompts. Above that, a seat is cheaper for Copilot Studio agents in Microsoft channels, and the seat also includes everyday AI in the Office apps. It doesn't cover Cowork, autonomous agents or Work IQ APIs. Use this break-even to target licenses at heavy users and leave light users on PAYG.

questions.question: A Copilot Studio agent with the Genie tool serves 5,000 unlicensed users, each asking 20 questions a month. Assuming each question is one agent action plus one generative answer, what's the Microsoft-side credit consumption?
choices: 0 credits, because Genie does the work on Databricks' side and Copilot Studio only relays the response
700,000 credits (5,000 × 20 × 7), about $7,000 PAYG, plus Databricks compute
100,000 credits (5,000 × 20 × 1), about $1,000 PAYG, plus compute
questions.explanation: Agent action (5) + generative answer (2) = 7 credits per question, so 100,000 questions is 700,000 credits ($7,000 PAYG, or 28 packs at $5,600 if steady). Retries, polling or extra tool calls add more. On the Databricks side, Genie AI usage is free through January 31, 2027, and SQL compute is billed. For licensed users in Microsoft channels the Microsoft side is no charge, so the license mix drives the model.

questions.question: A customer's Microsoft team proposes mirroring Unity Catalog into Fabric so Fabric data agents can answer questions in Copilot. Which point most directly protects governance?
choices: Fabric data agents can't be published to Teams or Microsoft 365 at all
Mirroring copies every table twice, once into OneLake and once into Dataverse, which doubles the customer's storage bill
Tables with row filters or masks, views and metric views don't mirror; Genie uses them in place
Mirroring requires an F64 capacity, which this customer doesn't have
questions.explanation: Fabric's mirroring limitations exclude tables with RLS or column-masking policies, plus views, metric views, federated and Delta Sharing tables. Mirroring is metadata plus shortcuts, not a full copy, and data agents run on F2+, so the other options are wrong. The governed, business-ready assets are the ones that don't make the trip. Genie keeps Unity Catalog in charge and still reaches Copilot through the plugin, the Teams app or Copilot Studio.

questions.question: Power Platform and Databricks are in different Entra tenants, so the Copilot Studio Genie connection must use a service principal. What's the main governance consequence?
choices: The agent's connection becomes read-write instead of read-only
Copilot Studio refuses to publish any agent that uses the connection
None, because Unity Catalog still receives each end user's identity through the service principal's token claims
Queries run as the service principal, so per-user Unity Catalog rules can't tell users apart
questions.explanation: OAuth (per-user) works only within one Entra tenant, and cross-tenant needs a service principal. Every user then gets the principal's access, so row filters keyed to the user can't tell users apart. Service principal Genie usage is also billed at standard PAYG, outside the free allowance. Grant the principal only the tables appropriate for everyone, or fix the tenant topology.

questions.question: Finance wants a hard monthly ceiling on Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go agent spend. They've set a budget on the PAYG billing policy. What should you tell them?
choices: Switch to P3, which automatically caps usage at the purchased amount
The PAYG billing policy budget is already a hard cap, so usage stops automatically when the figure is reached
That budget only alerts; use spending policies with a limited monthly budget for a cap
Hard spending caps aren't possible for any Microsoft AI service today
questions.explanation: Microsoft's PAYG setup page says the system doesn't enforce that budget. In Copilot Cost Management, a policy's limited monthly budget does cut users off until the first of the month, though enforcement is asynchronous. P3 is a discount commitment, not a cap. Defaults continue on PAYG when prepaid runs out.

questions.question: An MCA-E customer plans to buy a Copilot Credit P3 plan in February 2027 for the discount. What's the problem?
choices: P3 discounts end entirely in 2027 across every purchase channel
P3 requires a three-year term for any plan bought from 2027 onward
From Jan 1, 2027 P3 is EA or CSP only; MCA-E can't buy it and is pointed to AI Flex
Nothing changes for MCA-E customers, although P3 discounts drop by half for plans bought online after that date
questions.explanation: Microsoft's P3 page: starting January 1, 2027, P3 can be bought or renewed only via EA or a CSP partner, and MCA-E customers can't. The alternative is AI Flex, a broader commitment covering Copilot Credits, Foundry, GitHub AI and Security Copilot. Before any customer commits, check what that bundle locks in.

questions.question: A customer says, 'We bought Copilot for everyone, so our autonomous invoice-processing agent is free.' What's the right response?
choices: Autonomous runs consume credits even when every user is licensed, so budget for them
Correct, because a tenant where every user holds a Copilot license has no agent consumption to pay for at all
Correct, as long as the agent is published in Teams or Copilot Chat
Wrong, because autonomous agents are blocked in fully licensed tenants
questions.explanation: The licensed-user exemption depends on a licensed user interacting under their own identity. Event-triggered and autonomous runs have no such user, so they bill, and content processing (8 credits a page) or computer use can dominate. Model per-document cost before green-lighting automation.

questions.question: A customer plans to use Restricted SharePoint Search as their long-term Copilot oversharing control. How should you coach them?
choices: Proceed, because RSS is Microsoft's recommended permanent control and acts as a hard deny list for sensitive sites
Turn Copilot off instead, since there are no oversharing controls
RSS is retiring and was never a boundary; fix permissions, using RCD or RAC meanwhile
Rely on the semantic index, which hides sensitive files automatically
questions.explanation: RSS and RCD are temporary discovery controls that don't change permissions. The durable fix is permission hygiene: DAG reports to find EEEU and broad links, site access reviews delegated to owners, Restricted Access Control for sensitive sites, and labels with DLP. The same discipline (least privilege at the data layer) is what Unity Catalog enforces for Genie.

questions.question: A customer wants to move all 10,000 users to E7 so 'all the agent stuff is covered'. What's the most accurate coaching?
choices: E7 replaces the need for separate Purview, Defender and Entra investments
E7 must be bought for the whole tenant before Agent 365 can be used at all
E7 adds per-user components but no agent consumption; target it, since licenses can mix
E7 includes unlimited Copilot Credits for every licensed user, so it's the cheapest way to run agents at scale
questions.explanation: E7 ($99) is about $9 more than E5 + Copilot at list and adds Agent 365 and Entra Suite. It doesn't include Copilot Credits, Foundry consumption or Databricks costs. Microsoft confirms licenses can be mixed. Agent consumption still needs its own budget either way.

questions.question: An executive worries that bringing Genie into Copilot will let people see data they shouldn't. Which facts best address it?
choices: Genie answers are only visible to Databricks workspace admins
Each user signs in with their own Entra identity and Unity Catalog applies to every answer
Copilot strips all numbers out of Genie answers before showing them
Microsoft Purview re-checks every Genie answer against SharePoint permissions before Copilot is allowed to display it
questions.explanation: The plugin, Teams app and Cowork plugin all use the user's Entra sign-in with per-user connections, and each request runs with that user's permissions. Genie enforces Unity Catalog or source ACLs on every answer. Coach on artifact sharing (snapshots) and avoid service-principal shortcuts.

questions.question: A finance team wants one Teams agent that answers revenue questions from a curated Genie Agent, cites policy documents from SharePoint, and follows a custom approval flow. Which path fits best?
choices: The Azure Databricks Genie plugin in Copilot Chat, which supports SharePoint citations and custom approval flows on its own
A Copilot Chat (Basic) agent grounded only on public websites
A Fabric data agent built over a mirrored Unity Catalog catalog
A Copilot Studio agent with the Genie tool, SharePoint knowledge and an agent flow
questions.explanation: Copilot Studio combines a specific Genie Agent with Microsoft 365 knowledge and custom flows, branded and published to Teams. The costs: maker effort, a premium Power Apps license for the connection, the Managed MCP Servers preview, and Copilot Credits for unlicensed or autonomous use (agent flows bill unless triggered by 'When an agent calls the flow' for a licensed user).

questions.question: A customer's Copilot-licensed knowledge workers want to ask data questions in Copilot Chat with the least setup. Which Genie path does Databricks recommend?
choices: The Azure Databricks Genie plugin
Exporting Genie answers to SharePoint daily
A Copilot Studio agent per department
Building a custom engine agent in Foundry
questions.explanation: Databricks labels the plugin as the recommended option. Users install it from Plugins, enter the workspace hostname and sign in with Entra ID, with no @-mention needed. It requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and Genie One on the workspace, and it's in public preview with no VNet support.

questions.question: A US government (GCC) customer wants the Copilot Studio-to-Genie integration. What should you check first?
choices: Only whether the customer has bought Microsoft 365 E7, because the connector is included only in E7 for government tenants
Nothing. Every Genie integration path works the same way in GCC
The Power Platform Azure Databricks connector doesn't support government clouds
Whether the Databricks workspace uses serverless SQL warehouses
