questions.explanation: Databricks notes the Power Platform connector doesn't support government clouds. Check each integration path against the customer's cloud before proposing it.

questions.question: An EU customer asks where data flows when using the Genie Teams app. What's accurate?
choices: Data flows through Microsoft's Copilot service in the United States
A central service in East US 2 holds only the tenant mapping; processing follows Geo settings
Everything stays in the EU, with no exceptions for any component
All Genie queries and results are stored in East US 2 for 30 days, regardless of the workspace's region or Geo settings
questions.explanation: Databricks documents that the Teams app's central service runs in East US 2 and stores only the mapping, while content processing follows the workspace Geo setting. On the Microsoft side, note that Anthropic models are excluded from the EU Data Boundary. Document every hop for the DPO.

questions.question: A customer wants usage-based Copilot services rolled out deliberately, one at a time. Which default should they change?
choices: Enable Restricted SharePoint Search
Turn off Enterprise Data Protection
Disable the Microsoft 365 Copilot license for admins
Turn off 'Auto-apply new services' on spending policies
questions.explanation: Auto-apply new services is on by default, so new metered services join existing policies automatically. Turning it off means admins add each new service deliberately, which matters as Microsoft keeps adding metered experiences.

questions.question: A customer says, 'Copilot respects permissions, so we're safe to turn it on for everyone.' What's the coaching point?
choices: Oversharing only matters for external and guest users, not employees
Copilot will surface every existing overshare, so assess and fix permissions first
They're right. Respecting permissions makes oversharing impossible
They're right. Because Copilot respects permissions, it can't surface anything sensitive that users shouldn't be seeing
questions.explanation: Copilot shows users only what they can access, but in many tenants that's far too much ('Everyone Except External Users' links, broad sites). DSPM for AI's assessment and SAM's DAG reports find it, and access reviews and RAC fix it. The same applies to any agent, Genie included: the agent is only as well governed as the data layer.

questions.question: A pro-code team builds a Foundry agent that calls Genie through Databricks' managed MCP server. Which auth mode keeps Unity Catalog permissions per user?
choices: A shared API key
The Foundry project's managed identity
OAuth on-behalf-of (OBO)
Unauthenticated access inside a VNet
questions.explanation: Foundry supports key-based, Entra managed identity, OAuth OBO and unauthenticated MCP auth. Only OBO carries the end user's identity to Databricks so Unity Catalog applies row filters and masks per user. A managed identity makes every user look the same, and its usage bills like a service principal.

questions.question: A sponsor's business case prices Copilot at '$30 per user, all in.' Which planned use would break that assumption most?
choices: Drafting and rewriting customer emails in Outlook with Copilot every day, since each draft consumes Copilot Credits
Broad Cowork use for multi-step tasks, which bills Copilot Credits per task on top of the seat
Summarizing every Teams meeting and generating follow-up task lists
Asking web-grounded research questions in Copilot Chat all day
questions.explanation: Everyday AI (Office drafting, meeting summaries, chat) is included in the seat, subject to limits. Cowork needs both the license and usage-based billing, at roughly 100 to 700+ credits per task. A thousand users running a few tasks a week can match or exceed their seat costs.

questions.question: A customer has a large Azure MACC and worries that agent spend outside Microsoft won't count toward it. What's relevant for a Databricks-plus-Copilot strategy?
choices: Neither Copilot Credits nor Azure Databricks spend can count toward it
Only P3 counts toward MACC, and only for plans bought before 2027
Copilot Credits (PAYG or P3) decrement MACC, and Azure Databricks is Azure spend too
Only Microsoft 365 seat purchases count toward an Azure MACC; Copilot Credits and Azure Databricks spend never do
questions.explanation: Microsoft's credits guidance says PAYG and P3 Copilot Credits decrement MACC. Azure Databricks is a first-party Azure service billed through the customer's Azure subscription, so its consumption is Azure spend as well. Choosing Genie for analytics doesn't take money away from the Microsoft commitment.

questions.question: A customer's Copilot Studio usage swings between 40,000 credits in quiet months and 200,000 in quarter-end months. What's the problem with buying 8 capacity packs?
choices: Nothing, since unused credits from quiet months roll forward automatically and cover the quarter-end peaks
Packs don't roll over, so quiet months waste most of it; PAYG or P3 may fit better
Packs shrink automatically in quiet months, so there's no waste
Tenants can't hold more than five capacity packs at the same time
questions.explanation: 8 packs is 200,000 credits a month at $1,600. In a 40,000-credit month, 160,000 credits ($1,280) expire. Options: size packs to the baseline and let PAYG ($0.01) absorb peaks (agents aren't blocked), or use P3's annual pool. Also allocate capacity to critical environments so a quarter-end spike can't trigger 125% enforcement on them.
